title: [US] train_s1: shape, null rates, length distribution
headline: US slice of train_source1 is 1,323,633 rows (59.9792% of the 2,206,821-row file) and is immaculate on every integrity axis: name_empty=0, addr_empty=0, prefix_bad=0, len_hist sums exactly to rows. NEW corpus-level finding: addr_empty is IDENTICALLY ZERO for every country in both source-1 files (5 country-slices, 3,939,365 rows) and non-zero in all 10 source-2/3 slices - source 1 is not a random sample but a null-free template. A second independent field shows the same boundary: US dig6/row is 0.00125 here vs 0.01335-0.01430 in sources 2/3 (~11x collapse) while US dig5/row is flat, and US alpha_only_addr is exactly 1. This independently confirms the already_checked note that the pin gap bites US source-1, on a file that note did not cite.

most_important_number.meaning: US dig6/row collapse in source 1: 0.01393/0.00125 ~ 11x (train), 0.01335/0.00120 ~ 11x (test). The pin gate's country=='India' condition discards US 6-digit runs precisely in the source where they nearly vanish.
most_important_number.caveat: dig5/dig6 are OCCURRENCE counts, not row counts, so these are occurrences/row.

shape.country_sum_check: 1323633 + 883188 = 2206821 (100% of rows, no hidden third country)

null_rates_us.assessment: IMMACULATE. All three null/integrity fields are exact zeros. prefix_bad=0 is non-vacuous: build_profile.py:94 evaluates eid.startswith('S1-') per row, so 0/1323633 means the S1- prefix is a valid partition key for 100% of US rows. No prefix repair needed. has_digit_name at 2.606% is 2.4x lower than train_s3 (6.2981%), another source-dependent quantity.

new_finding_source1_partition.summary: addr_empty and dig6/row recomputed by this agent across ALL SIX profile files reveal an exact partition on the `source` field.

invariant_1.claim: addr_empty == 0 in EVERY source-1 country-slice, including France, and non-zero in ALL 10 source-2/3 country-slices.

invariant_2.claim: US dig6/row collapses ~11x in source 1 while US dig5/row stays flat, and India is flat on both. The collapse is US-and-6-digit specific, not general source-1 sparseness.

corroboration_alpha_only_addr.claim: US alpha_only_addr is exactly 1 row in each source-1 file vs 82467-184605 (4.2-6.1% of rows) in sources 2/3, while India is HIGH in source 1 (77036 = 8.7225%) and comparable throughout.
corroboration_alpha_only_addr.reading: Against build_profile.py:117 (if ba and not any(ch.isdigit() for ch in ba)), essentially every US source-1 address contains a digit and essentially no Indian one does - a generator difference consistent with the dig5/dig6 split.

lengths_us.dual_denominator_note: Because addr_empty = 0 here, the all-rows and non-empty denominators are IDENTICAL, so no dual-denominator caveat is needed (unlike P003/P005).
lengths_us.contrast: US addresses are shorter here than in train_s3 (34.96 vs 38.45 chars), US names too (22.47 vs 23.98). India is longer on both (26.39 name, 77.70 addr chars).

name_length_histogram_us.shape: Sharply unimodal - 45.4% in a single bucket - with a hard ceiling at 60-69. US train_s3 reached 80-89, so this file's US names are shorter-tailed.
name_length_histogram_us.consistency_check: Per-bucket min/max possible name_chars bound the total to [23717420, 35630117]; measured name_chars = 29735558 falls inside. Histogram and character total are mutually consistent.

sample_size.verdict: YES, decisively. Differences above ~0.2pp are real. The 11x dig6 gap is orders of magnitude beyond any sampling concern.
sample_size.scope_caveat: This file contains no France rows, so nothing here speaks to the only scored country.

interpretation.claim: Source 1 comes from a stricter generator than sources 2/3.
interpretation.basis: Four independent fields move together at the source boundary: addr_empty (0 vs 55k-111k), US dig6/row (~11x), US alpha_only_addr (1 vs 82k-185k), US has_digit_name (2.61% vs 6.30%). INFERENCE from the pattern: the source-1 template always emits a street number and a ZIP and never emits a missing field. The profile contains no generator information, so only the consequences are observable, not the template.

interpretation.claim: The pin gate is confirmed to bite US source-1, on a second file.
interpretation.basis: already_checked records dig6/row 0.001 for US source-1. I measure 0.00125 (train_s1) and 0.00120 (test_s1) vs 0.01335-0.01430 in US sources 2/3. What the note did NOT say, and this task adds, is that the effect is source-specific AND confined to the US: dig5 is unaffected and India is unaffected on both fields. The defect is precisely 'US source-1 addresses carry 5-digit ZIPs the India-only gate discards'.

interpretation.claim: The US comma invariant is exact here for a trivial reason.
interpretation.basis: has_comma = 1323633 = 100% because addr_empty = 0. The identity has_comma == rows - addr_empty therefore holds VACUOUSLY in source 1 - unlike in sources 2/3, it is not independent evidence of a fixed address template.

interpretation.claim: Do not extrapolate any null rate from this file to the corpus.
interpretation.basis: An agent profiling only source 1 would conclude the dataset has no missing addresses. It does not: 610,389 empty addresses exist across sources 2/3 (recomputed as the sum of addr_empty over all 10 source-2/3 country-slices; source-1 slices sum to exactly 0).

gaps.gap: Which source-1 rows lack a ZIP.
gaps.impact: dig5/dig6 are OCCURRENCE counts (len(findall(...)), build_profile.py:115-116), not row counts. 1656 is an upper bound on US source-1 rows carrying a standalone 6-digit run; 145393 an upper bound on 5-digit runs. Reported as occurrences/row, never row rates.
Distinct-row rates unavailable. Same gap P003 and P005 flagged; now the THIRD task to hit it, which is itself worth recording.

gaps.gap: The identity of the single alpha_only_addr US row.
gaps.impact: Can state that exactly one US address in this file contains no digit at all; cannot say what it is. Almost certainly a data-quality curiosity, not a defect.
normalize_address's output is never captured, so this speaks to the INPUT the gate would admit, not to rows that actually received a pin.

gaps.gap: No state / city / region field, and no component-count or component-position field.
gaps.impact: The component-order question raised in already_checked is unreachable from this profile.

gaps.gap: Whether the source-1 vs source-2/3 boundary has a nameable cause.
gaps.impact: The partition is provable; the attribution is not. Marked as inference rather than asserted.
The number of distinct businesses behind 1323633 rows is not derivable, nor the achievable ER target rate.

recommendations.action: Treat `source` as a stratification variable; never pool across it when reporting rates.
recommendations.expected_effect: Purely analytical. Prevents the most likely class of wrong conclusion from this dataset, namely reporting a corpus-level null rate that is really a sources-2/3 rate. No pipeline change.
recommendations.basis: addr_empty, US dig6/row, US alpha_only_addr and US has_digit_name all change discontinuously at the source-1 boundary.

recommendations.action: The pin gate defect now has two independent file-level measurements (train_s1 0.00125, test_s1 0.00120 vs 0.01335-0.01430).
recommendations.expected_effect: Raises confidence the fix belongs in the gate condition (normalize.py:337), not per-file special-casing. If widened to len(n) in (5,6), US rows in THIS file eligible for a pin blocking key rise from 1656 to at most 147049 (dig5 145393 + dig6 1656) - an upper bound on distinct rows, not a row rate. The commonly quoted 1656 -> 42321 comparison belongs to train_s3, not train_s1. Note the direction: source 1 is where the India-only gate discards the LEAST, so widening the gate helps sources 2/3 far more than source 1. The recall/precision tradeoff remains SPECULATIVE - no profile field measures the false-positive cost.

recommendations.action: No null handling, prefix repair, or name handling is warranted for US train_s1.
recommendations.expected_effect: None warranted. name_empty, addr_empty and prefix_bad are all exact zeros. Manufacturing a fix would be noise.

recommendations.action: No dictionary entry is warranted from this slice.
recommendations.expected_effect: None. This work order produced evidence about HOW ADDRESSES ARE GENERATED, not a missing normalisation token. No CONFIRMED/LIKELY/SPECULATIVE entries proposed.
P003 and P005 both treat has_comma == rows - addr_empty as evidence of a fixed address template. In source 1 it holds BECAUSE addr_empty = 0, so it proves nothing there.

refuted_findings.REFUTED-1_french_postcodes: Not re-derived, and my evidence does NOT support it. This file has no France rows. US dig5/row = 0.109844, consistent with the 0.110 quoted for the US, and the France figures in already_checked (0.004 in test_s1) stand unchallenged. What I add is the US source-1 correction the note flagged as already-covered, now measured on train_s1 as well.
refuted_findings.REFUTED-2_fr_regions_thin: Out of scope. train_source1 contains only US and India. No claim made.
